reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of the generative model stems from extending classical soccer models—specifically those using Poisson distributions—to college basketball. Each team is characterized by attack and defense coefficients, which are modeled as draws from gamma distributions. These coefficients are then used to predict scores via Poisson likelihood functions. The model is extended to incorporate conference-level variation by treating each team’s attack/defense as dependent on its conference. This introduces a hierarchical Bayesian structure where parameters vary across conferences. The model is evaluated not just on accuracy but also on profitability via simulated betting using Kelly’s criterion. The key insight is that while individual player contributions remain ambiguous, team-level latent factors can be reliably inferred and leveraged for prediction. The failure mode occurs when teams lack sufficient historical data or when match-ups are highly unpredictable due to external factors such as injuries or coaching changes.
